label: nxd-query-data-product + nxd-semantic-query-intent: unfiltered value probes, whole compound values, no unrequested filters (#451)
notes: Tightens filter discipline in the query and intent skills (unfiltered value probes, whole compound values, no unrequested filters). On the local-mesh semantic-filter-coverage scenario (Sonnet agent, 3 runs per arm, same mesh and nxd pin) both arms are indistinguishable: 2/3 passes each, with the only failing check being discovery-before-query (marker model not described) in one run per arm; the scenario does not discriminate the change on this model. The discriminating evidence is the nxd_eval gpt-6-luna arm-B result in PR #451 (16/20 -> 20/20).

checks.why: The final answer reports ALL=3, ALPHAVIR=2, ALPHAVIR SC=1 and BETAMAB=1, matching the trace's filtered query rows, and keeps ALL as a separate rollup row that should not be added to the product rows.
The trace shows a query with specialty_group IN ('Neurology','Psychiatry & Neurology') that returned exactly two rows, Psychiatry & Neurology=9 and Neurology=8, reported separately and not summed.
The agent reports NE Gulf Coast=7, NE Great Lakes=10 and SW Desert=4 from an unfiltered query grouped by region_name (filters_applied is empty, and the compiled SQL groups by REGION_NAME).

The filtered query on product_name=BETAMAB and region_name=SW Desert returned [0], and the agent reports it as a real zero without hedging, citing SW Desert=4 (visible in the region breakdown) and BETAMAB=7 overall (from its value probe).

The trace shows only a truncated list_models result and no visible describe_model call, and the agent announced and later reported describing just 'all three models', so the eval_enrollment_marker model exposed by the catalog was not described as the check requires.

The filters_applied output shows Q1 with region_name='NE Gulf Coast' and specialty_group='Psychiatry & Neurology', Q2 with specialty_group IN the two values, Q3 grouped by region_name with no filter, and Q4 with product_name='BETAMAB' and region_name='SW Desert'.
Every query went through the run_semantic_query MCP tool with concept-name arguments; the query_sql.py script was never called, and the only SQL visible is the compiled_sql the tool returned.

verdict.summary: All four answers are correct and their scopes appear in the tool-call filters, but the discovery check fails because the trace shows no describe_model call for every model, including the catalog's marker model; the agent said it described only three models.
